**Company Description**

Robert Bosch Produktie N.V., located in Tienen, Belgium, is within the Bosch Group the lead plant and worldwide center of competence for development, engineering and manufacturing of wiper arms. Customers are both original equipment automotive car manufactures and aftermarket customers. As part of the Bosch strategy, we offer students the opportunity to participate in an internship at our location. Safety, Cost efficiency and quality are our main focus points, and to maintain the excellent position we are at, we strive for: continuous improvement of our equipment efficiency, proactive work on process understanding and root cause analysis, introduction of new process and process automatisation to reduce manufacturing cost and introduction of new products to improve customer satisfaction.

If you look for a position where you can take initiative, learn and bring added value in an industrial environment, you’re the student we are looking for. The internship will ideally last 3-6 months and can be either full-time or part-time (let us know your availability, and we’ll work something out). At present, you can work remotely.

**Job Description**

Depending on your study program the internship may contain the following main points:

* Support the design of new production machines and processes
* Participation in Bosch Production System Projects
* Lean Manufacturing
* Value Stream planning
* Continuous Improvement work on existing manufacturing lines in the fields of Quality, Failure Cost, Safety, Environment, Ergonomics, …
* Data collecting and capability calculation
* I4.0 and digitalization
* Paperless projects
* Automatisation of administrative workflows
* Automated reporting of connected machines i.e. power BI
* On condition and depending on the ongoing projects, support of larger manufacturing projects regarding:

o Design and develop a new assembly line for a future wiper generation

o Simulate the different workplaces with time analysis

o Find solutions for the different design topics and perform cost comparisons in team

o Participation in the entire project from first draft until implementation

**Qualifications**

. You must be enrolled as a student.

* Language: good knowledge of English is required. German and possibly Dutch is a plus

. Fields of study: mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, production engineering, technical business economics.

* Completed basic study period
* Good knowledge of MS-Office
* You are able to communicate, you can work on your own as well as work as a teamplayer
* Responsible, independent and reliable worker
* Intercultural interest and understanding

An internship will be successful if you are inquisitive, active and ask for work.

The main condition is that you are a European citizen and if not, you can only do an internship through a European exchange program.

**Additional Information**

The internship requires that you have the nationality of a EU-country or that you are taking part in the Erasmus program.

The personal experience of the interns is usually the following: The company employs 10-15 interns all year round from various countries. Therefore this is also a great opportunity to enhance your social and language skills. The interns live mostly in Tienen or in Leuven, known as a multicultural university city. You receive 800 € as expense reimbursement per month.

**Ref.: BE-IP-2026-02**

**I****nternship Proposal**

**Improvement of the simulation tool to predict the cure-induced deformation of composite parts**

Cenaero, located in Gosselies (Belgium), is an applied research center providing to companies involved in a technology innovation process high fidelity numerical simulation methods and tools to invent and design more competitive products.

Cenaero's ambition is to be internationally recognized as a technology leader in modeling and numerical simulation, to be a strategic partner of large global industries as well as a real support to regional companies including innovative SME. Mainly active in Aeronautics, Cenaero wishes to increase the transfer and the application of its technology to surface transport, energy, health and sustainable development. Cenaero operates a top supercomputing infrastructure TIER-1 among the world 500 most powerful systems.

Cenaero research and engineering teams focus on modeling of manufacturing processes (Additive manufacturing, welding, machining, etc), structures and high-tech materials design and integrity analysis, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and multi-disciplinary optimization (MDO).

One of the main axis of the High Performance Composite (HPComp) team is the process modeling. The HPComp team primarily focuses on the development of cutting edge numerical tools capable of predicting the response of composite structures and simulating their manufacturing processes. These tools can be used to develop more competitive products and/or manufacturing processes. The present proposal deals with the modeling of the cure-induced deformations of composite parts.

**Context**

The polymerisation reaction, or curing, which brings the liquid thermoset resin to solid, induces internal stresses within the part being produced. During this change of state, the part deforms due to thermal expansion and chemical shrinkage of the resin. The contact conditions with the mould and/or the pressure exerted on the part prevent these deformations from developing freely and internal stresses build up. Upon demoulding, part of the internal stresses is released, resulting in the appearance of distortions. Modeling such process involve complex coupled thermo-chemico-mechanical simulations. The curing simulation are performed at Cenaero via a User Material Subroutines used through a FE commercial software, Abaqus or Samcef.

**Objective**

The tool-part and inter-plies interactions are known to have a significant impac.t on the cure-induced deformation of composite parts. In order to avoid the costly and complex experimental characterization of those interaction laws parameters, Cenaero will use its own multi-disciplinary optimization platform called Minamo. The objective is to use Minamo to fit the parameters required to the model.

The internship offered will require the student: (i) to familiarize him/herself with the User Material Subroutine written in Python by Cenaero, (ii) familiarize with Minamo, (iii) set up the optimization chain to fit the parameters required for the interplies and tool-part interaction laws. A detailed report of the internship activities will need to be provided at the end of the internship.

**Duration**

The length of the internship can range between 4 and 6 months. The intern is required to work full time at Cenaero premises.

**Contact**

Interested candidates should send a cover letter, quoting reference number of the offer (BE-IP-2026-02), and a resume to rh\_be-ip-2026-02@cenaero.be

In a nutshell:

At **Toyota Motor Europe** in **Zaventem**, this internship in the NV & Driveability team focuses on virtual development of road noise. The intern will analyse tire, rim, and suspension vibration modes, optimize assessment methods, validate simulations with CAE tools, and support physical testing to reduce vehicle cabin noise and improve driving comfort.

Company Information:

Toyota is one of the world’s largest automobile manufacturers and a leading global company, founded in 1937. Today, Toyota sells vehicles in 170 countries and employs over 350,000 people worldwide.
At Toyota Motor Europe (TME), with our headquarters based in Brussels, Belgium, around 2,700 colleagues from more than 60 nationalities work together across Europe. We are responsible for the wholesale marketing of Toyota and Lexus vehicles, parts and accessories, and we support Toyota’s European R&D, manufacturing, and engineering operations.
We are on an exciting journey as we continue to evolve into a mobility company. Our goal is to create even more value and happiness for our customers through a wide range of mobility solutions.

Your team and your responsibilities:

**Team/division description**

TME R&D centre is responsible for planning, development and production support of vehicles aimed at - and locally produced for - the European market.

The “NV & Driveability” team is part of the Vehicle Performance Engineering division (VPE) division and is responsible for the vehicle NVH (Noise, Vibration and harshness) according to EU customer expectations. We aim at the development of attractive and “fun to drive” cars matching European market requirements and customer expectations. Using state-of-the art experimental and numerical methods, we develop strategies to achieve the targets and validate them on virtual and physical prototypes.

**Your project**

Tire rolling noise, or road noise, is one of the main sources of noise in modern cars, becoming more impactful on customer expectations with the increased share of hybrid and electric powertrains. To achieve a low level of road noise in the vehicle cabin, the forces entering the vehicle body through the suspension must be minimised. An important aspect is the control of the different modes in the tire, rim, and suspension. By transitioning to the virtual development of these components, we can accelerate time-to-market while simultaneously lowering CO2 emissions and reducing costs.

You will contribute to an ongoing research project where the main goal is to build a detailed understanding of the different modes along the road noise path, how they contribute to the force transmission, and how they can be controlled through specific properties of the components involved. You will:

* Optimize the existing procedures for component/subassembly mode assessment.
* Validate findings and support component/subassembly development through CAE software.
* Confirm findings by physical component/subassembly updates.

Your Profile:

You are pursuing your master’s in mechanical or automotive engineering, with a strong interest in cars and sound/acoustics. You have a background in structural dynamics (including modal analysis) and acoustics; knowledge of Noise & vibration testing (Testlab) and simulation (Nastran) is an important plus. You have some affinity with mathematical and physical modelling, and scientific scripting in Matlab or Python. You have a good English capability, and you are eager to work in a multi-cultural environment.

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Join AWS and help operate one of the world's most advanced cloud infrastructures serving European customers. As an intern on our Managed Operations team, you'll gain hands-on experience building, operating, and improving critical cloud services like EC2, S3, Lambda, and Bedrock. You'll work alongside experienced engineers to solve real operational challenges, contribute to system reliability and performance, and develop practical skills in cloud operations that will shape your career in technology.

Execute changes to production systems following established change management processes and operational procedures
Collaborate with team members to resolve operational issues and improve system reliability

Your internship focuses on the operational excellence of the European Sovereign Cloud, a specialized AWS infrastructure serving EU customers. You'll spend your time monitoring the health of large-scale distributed systems, investigating anomalies to understand root causes, and documenting findings in actionable reports. description:
**Build health technology that changes lives.**

Join Resmed as an **Intern, Product Development, Devices Software** and be part of a team developing technology that helps people sleep, breathe, and live better lives.

Based onsite in our Sandyford, Dublin office, this six-month internship offers the opportunity to contribute directly to product development projects while working alongside software engineers, biomedical algorithm engineers, technologists, and data scientists.

You will gain hands-on exposure to the development of connected healthcare products, take ownership of your own work, and help bring innovative solutions to market that improve the lives of millions of people worldwide.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Work within one of Resmed's software engineering teams focused on device development.
* Contribute to software development activities across multiple platforms and technology stacks.
* Support the design and development of new products, enhancements, and product improvements.
* Collaborate with engineers, developers, and cross-functional stakeholders to understand customer and business needs.
* Participate in product development projects that bring healthcare technologies to market.
* Take ownership of assigned work activities and deliverables.
* Communicate project outcomes clearly to internal and external stakeholders.
* Help translate technical requirements into effective software solutions.
Contribute to a team culture focused on innovation, quality, and customer impact.

**What You Bring**
------------------

* Currently studying toward a degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
* Programming capability in languages such as Python, Java, or C++.
* Clear written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to explain complex information in a simple and compelling way.
* Interest in software development across different technologies and platforms.
* Ability to understand technical challenges and contribute to problem-solving.
Collaborative approach and willingness to learn in a team environment.

*Nice to Have*

* Interest in healthcare technology or connected devices.
* Exposure to more than one programming language.
Academic or personal projects demonstrating software development skills.

**What Sets You Apart**
-----------------------

* **Curiosity** : Enjoys exploring new technologies, ideas, and ways of solving problems.
* **Creative Thinking** : Approaches challenges with fresh perspectives and innovative solutions.
* **Ownership** : Takes responsibility for deliverables and follows through on commitments.
* **Resilience** : Remains composed and effective when priorities or challenges change.
* **Drive** : Brings energy, initiative, and a willingness to go the extra mile when needed.
* **Team Spirit** : Values collaboration and contributes positively to shared goals.

**Why Join Resmed**
-------------------

At Resmed, our mission is to help millions of people sleep, breathe, and live better lives. As a global leader in connected devices and digital health, we develop technologies that support people living with sleep apnoea, COPD, and other chronic respiratory diseases. You will join a business driven by innovation, purpose, and customer impact, while working alongside experts across software engineering, data science, and healthcare technology.

This internship offers the chance to work on meaningful products, gain hands-on development experience, and learn in a supportive, inclusive environment where diverse perspectives and new ideas are valued. Here, you'll contribute to work that matters while building skills that will support your future career.

**Practical Details**

* Location: Sandyford, Dublin (onsite)

* Duration: 6 months, starting January 2026

* Application deadline: Friday, October 23rd 2026 COB.

Selection process: Hirevue video, TA Partner phone call, onsite interview with the Product team

#LI-EU

Joining us is more than saying “yes” to making the world a healthier place. It’s discovering a career that’s challenging, supportive and inspiring. Where a culture driven by excellence helps you not only meet your goals, but also create new ones. We focus on creating a diverse and inclusive culture, encouraging individual expression in the workplace and thrive on the innovative ideas this generates. If this sounds like the workplace for you, apply now! We commit to respond to every applicant.

About us
Today, 7 out of 10 people globally lack access to life-saving Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). Conventional MRI machines are massive, cost millions of euros, and require specialized, shielded rooms which means they are usually confined to large hospitals.
At DeepSpin, we are changing that by building the World’s First Flatbed MRI.
Our open-architecture scanner plugs into a standard wall socket, fits into regular doctor's offices, and costs 10x less than conventional systems.
Backed by globally leading VCs, we are expanding our team in Berlin. This is an opportunity to join a mission-driven team bringing an essential medical technology to the billions of people who currently cannot afford it.
About Position
At DeepSpin, you will be supporting the R&D team. As a working student in Engineering, you will be part of our rapidly growing team with 20 h/week in a variety of tasks including:
Participate in the assembly and construction of electromechanical components for our MRI prototype.
Collaborate with team members to ensure components meet design specifications.
Assist in troubleshooting and diagnosing issues with custom-built components and systems.
Work closely with engineers to identify root causes of problems and implement effective solutions.
Assist in the procurement,sourcing and quality management of electromechanical components for our MRI system
Research and evaluate potential suppliers and vendors.
Requirements
Student of Electronics / Mechatronics Engineering or a comparable course of study, with residence in Berlin
Excellent communication skills and a proactive get-stuff-done attitude
First principles thinking when diagnosing problems and applying research to a commercial setting
Passion for impactful projects and for revolutionising the healthcare market with us
Preferred: experience in a lab-like setting: designing, measuring and troubleshooting complex technical solutions
What we offer
Dynamic & Innovative Culture: A creative workplace with flat hierarchies and open communication among a highly skilled collaborative team
International environment: A diverse and multicultural English-first office with more than 10 different nationalities driven by the same purpose, to revolutionize medical imaging
Benefits: Urban Sports Club, BVG and lifestyle vouchers along with company-sponsored lunch in our penthouse office and monthly team events
Personal development: In addition to learning on the job through mentorship and high responsibility from the start, we encourage and support personal development (trainings, certifications etc.)
Work-life balance: Flexible working hours + 30 days of paid leave per year and Parental leaves.

description:
What we do
We invest in companies building at the frontier of AI. We think a fund that does that should run on the same stack it funds, so we automate our own work instead of hiring more people to do it manually.
Today a lot of our operating layer is still hand-rolled: dealflow arrives by inbox and LinkedIn and gets triaged by humans, deal notes and call transcripts live in places nobody searches, LP and portfolio reporting is assembled by hand every quarter. Each of those is an automation problem, and nobody currently owns them.
That's the job. You will own building the internal systems that make this fund faster working directly with our partners, shipping to real users (us) from week one.
This is not a traditional VC internship. You will not be building comp tables.
Your role
What you will have shipped
An automated dealflow triage layer:
inbound opportunities enriched, screened against our thesis, and routed into our CRM without a human doing the first pass.
A working internal knowledge system:
our meeting transcripts, deal notes and memos actually searchable and queryable by the team.
A team of internal agents in daily use
by the investment team, in investor relations, dealflow evaluation, portfolio support, or reporting.
A documented view of where our operating layer goes next:
what you'd build with another six months, and what other leading funds are already doing that we aren't.
We'll agree the specific list with you in week one. What's fixed is the bar: things that get used, not prototypes that get demoed once.
Your profile
You own what you do and you are comfortable driving this effort.
You build things that work. Python, APIs, LLM/agent frameworks, and whatever glue gets it done including no-code where that's the right call.
You ship end-to-end and unsupervised. Nobody will hand you a spec; you'll find the bottleneck, propose the fix, and build it.
You care whether it's still running next month. Hacky is fine; unmaintainable is not.
You can talk to non-engineers about their own workflows, and get a busy investor to actually adopt what you built.
You're available for at least 3 months, ideally 6, onsite in Berlin, and you can work in English.
Helps, but we'll teach you:
experience with CRM or reporting infrastructure (we use Attio); prior startup, VC or founder experience; a background in Computer Science or Engineering.
You don't need
any prior finance or VC experience. If you've automated your way out of a job before, that's the signal we're looking for.
What we offer
Our hierarchy is flat and communication direct, which means that we operate and learn fast, as a team. Our team and work environment can be described as follows:
We have an entrepreneurial mindset: we are creative, focused, ambitious, and not easily discouraged;
We work in a fast-paced, highly innovative environment where ambiguity is the norm;
We work independently but have a cooperative mindset;
We love what we do and we own it.
In addition to a competitive salary, you can expect the following:
Real ownership of a workstream that a partner cares about, and daily contact with the people running the fund.
A front-row seat to European AI dealflow - the companies, the founders, and the technology.
The Merantix ecosystem: AI Campus Berlin, Merantix Momentum, the London AI Hub, AI House Davos, and a network of founders, AI researchers and industry partners.
A competitive salary, flexible hours, and a flat structure where you talk directly to whoever can unblock you.
Regular team events as well as fun team colleagues

description:
Who we are - Our Mission
terralayr addresses the massive deficit in global energy storage.
The over-indexing of electricity generation from renewable energy sources leads to large volatility on the energy grid. The main problem is that wind and solar farms are fluctuating and, by definition, unsteady—there is no sun at night, and it is not always windy. This increases the need for flexibility in the form of battery storage systems to balance the grid in times when supply and demand do not match.
By buying and developing grid-scale storage assets and virtually aggregating them across a layer, we are creating the world's first energy cloud. Imagine AWS for energy. Through the flexibility we secure, we can market flexibility-as-a-service and hedging products/power insurance to utilities, SMEs, and industrial players and create virtual storage capacity for PV and wind farms.
What we are hiring for - Your Role
We are looking for a
Strategy & Commercial Intern (m/f/d)
to join our team for a period of ideally 6 months. This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in business development, market analysis, and supporting commercial initiatives within a dynamic and fast-paced environment.
What you will work on - Your Responsibilities
Support the Chief Commercial Officer
, contributing to strategic initiatives and ensuring seamless execution of commercial activities.
Facilitate and manage the customer acquisition process
, including contract preparation, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement.
Create commercial materials
such as sales decks, market analyses, and proposals, and actively participate in partner calls.
Support contract execution
by preparing proposals, presentations, and organizing data rooms, ensuring accurate and timely delivery.
Contribute to product ideation and evaluation
, assisting in product development processes and analyzing commercial implications.
Provide administrative support
to the team as needed.
What we are looking for - Your Qualifications
Education:
You are currently pursuing or already have a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Economics, or any comparable subject from a top tier university or business school and are looking for an internship, ideally 6 months.
Experience:
You have first work experience in demanding, fast-paced environments (e.g., consulting, investment banking, startups, etc.).
You are a team player, have a hands-on mentality and organisational skills.
Mindset:
You are proactive and have a self-starter mindset with excellent organisational, interpersonal and analytical skills.
You thrive in ambiguity
and don’t crack under the pressure of a demanding environment.
Any previous experience in energy markets
or in the development and operation of renewable energy assets are a plus.
Why you should be excited about this opportunity
Working for a company with a clear mission
: A world powered by 100% renewable energy.
Get first-hand experience
by working closely with experienced entrepreneurs and senior team members who support your development through mentoring.
A steep learning curve
combined with a lot of space to bring in your own ideas and shape terralayr’s future.
A strong team culture
and lively interactions with the team.

**DESCRIPTION**

Important — Site Location & Commuting: This role is based at a data center facility in a remote location with no public transportation access. A valid driving license and access to personal transportation are required to commute to the site daily. Please consider this before applying.

Ever wanted to help design and support the data centers that power the world's largest cloud? As a DC Infra Engineer Intern at Amazon Web Services (AWS), you will work alongside an experienced, cross-disciplinary team to provide full life-cycle support to AWS data centers — from design inception through site improvement and maintenance. Your work will directly impact millions of customers worldwide.

Each day, you will interact with different teams responsible for all aspects of the data centers. You will help prioritize activities that support data center capacity, availability, and safety, focusing on the actions that are most impactful — and you will have the opportunity to work on projects both locally and globally. If this sounds exciting to you, come build the future with us!

This internship is designed as a potential pathway to full-time employment. Interns who demonstrate strong performance throughout their internship may be considered for a full-time engineering position, subject to available roles and business needs.

Who Should Apply

We welcome applications from:

* Students in the last year of their Bachelor's or Master's degree (graduating 2027) in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Architecture, Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related technical discipline, who are looking for an internship that could lead to a full-time career.

About the Role

As an intern, you will engage with an experienced cross-disciplinary staff to provide full life-cycle support to AWS data centers, from design through operation. With guidance from experienced engineers, you will build your subject matter expertise and serve as an engineering resource for your region, applying what you learn to real technical challenges.

You will be exposed to both independent work and team-based collaboration. Prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to being successful.

What You Will Do – Are these job responsibilities accurate for the internship?

* Perform design and equipment submittal reviews for new data centers in your region
* Troubleshoot issues, conduct Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and create Corrective Action (CA) documentation for site and equipment failures
* Support operational issues with ad-hoc training, complex operating procedure reviews (including for critical equipment), and event support
* Collaborate with the internal data center design engineering team, server hardware team, and environmental health and safety team to promote standards that maintain consistency and reliability in services delivered
* Work on concurrent projects, sometimes across multiple geographical regions

Internship Structure

Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours per week) for 12 consecutive weeks, starting 2027. This position requires the intern to report to work on site daily. Intern schedules are typically day schedules, Monday to Friday.

description:
At Materialise Medical, we believe that better healthcare starts with solutions designed around the individual patient. If you’re passionate about bringing personalized care to every patient, you’ll love being a part of this team. Through the technology we develop, researchers, engineers, and clinicians are revolutionizing personalized treatment — helping improve and save lives daily.

This internship focuses on developing an experimental and computational approach to evaluate the mechanical behavior of a novel implant design under clinically relevant loading conditions. The work will involve material characterization of implant materials, creation of a simplified phantom model with relevant mechanical characteristics, mechanical characterization of the implant under relevant clinical loads and creation and validation of a simplified computational model.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* **Material characterization**
Testing and analysis of tensile and compressive properties of different 3DP materials. The intern will define the optimum material properties and give input to Materialise on the optimum material and printer combinations .
* **Creation of simplified phantom model**
The work will include the selection of suitable materials for constructing a simplified anatomical phantom that can reproduce relevant mechanical characteristics. The intern will then design and fabricate the phantom.
* **Mechanical characterization of the implant**
The intern will implant selected implant designs within the phantom model and apply controlled loads representative for the clinical reality. The experimental study will assess implant deformation, retained shape changes, and possible failure modes. These results should provide insight into how the surrounding environment influences implant response compared with stand-alone mechanical testing.
* **Computational modelling**
Finally, the intern will develop simplified finite element models of the phantom–implant system. The models will be used to simulate and predict implant deformation. The experimental data will then be used to validate and refine the simulations.

The outcome of the internship will be a combined experimental–numerical workflow that supports the selection of worst-case testing conditions, improves understanding of implant, and contributes to the development of future implant verification strategies.

**Profile**
-----------

* Mechanical, biomedical or material engineering background with a strong interest in both experimental and computational characterization of 3D printed medical devices
* Must be able to provide a university internship contract (no internships after graduation).

**About the project:**

The *Frontal Leaf* project aims to develop a next-generation resorbable implant for surgical care following advanced sinus surgery. During the first project year, the focus is on polymer formulation development, implant manufacturing, drug incorporation, implantation validation, sterilization studies, cytocompatibility studies and preparation for subsequent preclinical evaluation.

**About the team:**

The Frontal Leaf project is led by Prof. Thibaut Van Zele (Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Ghent University Hospital), Prof. Peter Dubruel and Bryan Bogaert (Polymer Chemistry & Biomaterials Group, Ghent University) combining internationally recognized expertise in biomaterials, polymer technologies and advanced sinus surgery.

The project is further backed by a multidisciplinary valorisation team bringing together the expertise from ChemTech (Dr. Valentina Goftman) and MedTeG (Dr. Gilles Brackman).

**Key responsabilities:**

· Develop and optimize polymer formulations for processing starting from ready-to-use building blocks.

· Evaluate the physicochemical properties of the formulations including rheological profile, solidification kinetics and mechanical performance.

· Incorporate APIs into the formulation and investigate the distribution and elution thereof in a relevant physicochemical environment.

· Evaluate the impact of different sterilization strategies on polymer performance.

· Collaborate with engineering partners and evaluate proposed models.

· Perform biocompatility assays following ISO 10993 protocols.

· Support protocol development, documentation and planning for upcoming *in vivo* validation.

**Required qualifications:**

· Master’s degree in biomedical sciences, biomedical engineering, bio-engineering, biotechnology or related fields.

· Strong written and verbal skills in English and preferably Dutch.

· Highly recommended to have obtained the license to draft and hand in ethical files (“proefdierkunde”).

· Strong interest in biomaterials, drug delivery systems and medical device development.

· Excellent experimental and organizational skills as well as outstanding laboratory documentation skills.

· Ability to perform work independantly within the context of an interdisciplinary team.

**What we offer:**

· One-year full time research position at Ghent university.

· Possibility to apply for a 4 year full scholarship from FWO following this project.xpertise in polymer science and technology transfer.

· Collaborative experience across clinical, industrial, and engineering environments, with expertise in polymer science and technology transfer.

· Rare look into translational work from research environment to patients.

· Opportunity to develop skills within biological, chemical and engineering fields.

· A stimulating research environment at the interface of biomaterials, drug delivery, and medical device innovation.

description:
High-performance MEMS gyroscopes are essential for modern applications ranging from consumer electronics to robotics. While initial calibration handles manufacturing tolerances, environmental factors such as temperature changes, mechanical stress and ageing can cause performance drift over time. To maintain long-term accuracy, this project focuses on developing, as well as validating efficient, non-intrusive system identification methods. Instead of relying on complex hardware modifications, as part of your Master thesis, you will explore innovative techniques for injecting test signals directly into the system in order to identify key parameters. You will develop and evaluate innovative concepts for injecting test signals for in-field parameter identification. In addition, you will design and set up test scenarios to validate the developed methods. Last but not least, you will apply your system identification algorithms, benchmark their performance quantitatively and assess their suitability for sensor platforms.

Education: Master studies in the field of Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Physics, Embedded Systems, Microsystems Technology or comparable Experience and Knowledge: a strong understanding of control systems, signal processing and system identification experience with laboratory equipment, as well as microcontrollers is a plus knowledge of MEMS sensor fundamentals or gyroscopes is a major advantage Personality and Working Practice: you are an enthusiastic and creative individual who is genuinely willing to collaborate with international, as well as interdisciplinary teams Work Routine: your on-site presence is required Languages: very good in English

Cette approche consiste donc à prendre en compte simultanément tous les phénomènes et considérations dimensionnants du système, identifier leurs interactions et les formaliser explicitement afin de les inclure dans un processus d’optimisation. Intégrer les solutions de simplification des calculs s'appuyant sur des approches multi échelle déjà existantes. Formuler et implémenter un processus d'optimisation permettant de minimiser la masse des pièces considérées tout en leur assurant une tenue mécanique suffisante afin de les mettre en œuvre sur des cas concrets à complexité croissante.

Rattaché·e au département Structures au sein de la direction technique, en lien étroit avec les référents métiers, ingénieur·e·s calculs, lead calculs ainsi qu’avec le département innovation concernant les caractérisations matériaux, vous contribuez au développement des sujets de qualification mécanique des solutions membranaires GTT dédiées aux navires transporteurs de GNL. L’amélioration continue de nos méthodes de validation est un enjeu majeur pour fournir à nos clients des solutions efficaces, économes et sûres, dans des délais toujours plus contraints. Dans cette perspective, nous souhaitons industrialiser une nouvelle méthode de calcul thermomécanique permettant de prédire de manière fiable l’état de contrainte au sein de nos systèmes d’isolation. Cette approche, fondée sur la prise en compte du comportement visqueux des différents constituants du système, a déjà fait l’objet d’une première mise en œuvre lors des phases d’avant-projet. S’appuyant sur une compréhension approfondie des mécanismes de déformation élastique et visqueuse, elle offre à terme la possibilité de définir des critères de validation spécifiquement adaptés aux zones les plus sensibles de la cuve. Cette approche ouvre la voie au développement de nouveaux panneaux préfabriqués dont la conception tire pleinement parti du comportement viscoélastique intrinsèque des matériaux. Elle permet ainsi de réduire efficacement les surcontraintes d’origine thermique tout en préservant un niveau optimal de performance thermique. L’approche proposée est modulable et s’articule autour de deux volets : Volet calcul : Développer une méthodologie de calcul incrémental viscoélastique applicable aux matériaux pour lesquels cette approche est particulièrement pertinente, tels que les mousses et les colles. Cette méthodologie sera ensuite déployée sur une base de données de projets réalisés afin d’évaluer les marges de conservatisme des conceptions actuelles et de quantifier les gains potentiels associés. Volet exploratoire : Proposer une version optimisée du panneau isolant tirant pleinement parti du comportement visqueux des matériaux afin de favoriser la relaxation des contraintes induites par la mise en froid. Cette conception sera développée en collaboration avec le département Innovation de GTT et s’appuiera sur les connaissances et le retour d’expérience acquis sur les mousses isolantes.

description:
Electric drives are at the heart of modern mechatronics, and the industry is rapidly moving toward sensorless control to estimate rotor positions using software rather than physical sensors. This thesis explores how Artificial Intelligence and Neural Networks can revolutionize traditional control architectures. The goal is to investigate and design advanced neural network concepts that learn control and estimation tasks. By mapping system measurements to control states, this research aims to pave the way for the next generation of intelligent, software-defined electric drive control. During your thesis you will gain a solid understanding of the physical models of electric drives (e.g., electric machines, inverters) and the simulation environment. You will analyze state-of-the-art machine learning and neural network approaches applied to sensorless control of electric drives. Furthermore, you will develop novel AI-based control architectures, exploring both modular and end-to-end neural network designs. You will implement, test, and validate your control algorithms using high-fidelity electric drive simulation models. Finally, you will document your methodology, analyze the results, and present your findings to the development team.

Rattaché·e au Département Structure de la Direction Technique, vous contribuez au développement de méthodologies liées au dimensionnement du Containment System (CS) des cuves de stockage cryogénique du gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL). Ces cuves équipent principalement les méthaniers, mais également des navires propulsés au GNL. Dans le cadre des études portées sur le CS Mark III, GTT souhaite affiner ses méthodologies de calcul, notamment pour obtenir des prédictions plus précises, voire lever certains conservatismes. Pour cela, vous serez amené·e à intégrer les dernières lois de comportement et éléments de modélisation dans les modèles d’études existants. Ces études sont basées sur des calculs éléments finis (solveur Abaqus) de sous-systèmes CS. Les chargements considérés dans ces calculs sont dus aux différentes sollicitations dans la cuve, telles que le thermique, les déformations coque et les pressions de cargaison. On s’intéressera particulièrement aux zones spéciales du CS. Vous aurez à établir un plan de validation pour les différentes zones à traiter en considérant les cas de charge pertinents. Les réponses étudiées sont les déformations, les contraintes dans le CS et les coefficients de sécurité résultants. Il faudra quantifier l’apport de chaque piste de modélisation en comparaison aux modèles actuels et développer des méthodologies de calculs associées. Le stage sera réalisé en étroite collaboration avec le Département Matériaux de la Direction de l’Innovation, notamment pour l’établissement des lois matériaux.

description: Ever wondered how industrial print systems are made faster, smarter and more compact? Are you interested in tuning control loops, improving experimental hardware and programming real mechatronic systems in a professional R&D environment? Your assignment - context Large-format print systems are used to produce applications such as posters, banners, self-adhesive graphics and wallpaper. Within Canon Production Printing we continuously explore new ways to add value to printed output and to extend what our industrial inkjet systems can do. In this assignment you will work on embellishment processes that are being used for large format printing. The current setup demonstrates the principle, but the next step is to bring the process towards full platform speeds while making the hardware concept more compact, robust and controllable. The challenge is strongly mechatronic; examples are thin film handling, web transport, cartridge design, tension control, actuator behavior, sensor feedback and process timing all interact. You will investigate how the present hardware and control strategy can be improved, and you will validate your ideas through experiments on a dedicated test setup. The specifics of your assignment may include • Characterizing the current embellishment setup and identifying speed-limiting mechanisms in web handling, thin film handling, tension control and process synchronization. • Tuning and improving control loops, web/thin film tension or actuator timing, using experimental data and system-identification thinking. • Improving the hardware concept to support higher process speeds and a more compact machine layout, including sensor selection, mounting/cartridge concepts, mechanical adaptations and cable/signal routing. • Programming and adapting control or data-acquisition software for experimentation, logging, visualization and repeatable test execution. • Designing and executing experiments to quantify process stability, repeatability, operating window and failure modes at increasing speed. • Translating the findings into practical design recommendations for the next iteration of the embellishment process. Research areas • High-speed web and media handling: determine which mechanical or dynamic effects become dominant when moving towards full print speeds. • Control-loop performance: improve speed, stability and disturbance rejection without making the system overly sensitive or difficult to tune. • Compact hardware design: explore how the present setup can be simplified, integrated or redesigned while maintaining accessibility for tests and maintenance. • Process robustness: study what causes wrinkles, slip, tension peaks, misalignment or unstable transfer, and determine how to detect or prevent these issues. • Experimental validation: create a practical test approach with clear KPIs, logging, comparison methods and recommendations for follow-up development. Lieu : 7C place du Dôme - 92800 PARIS LA DEFENSE. Durée et/ou période du stage : 4 à 6 mois, 1er semestre 2027. En tant que stagiaire, vous serez intégré(e) au sein de la Direction Technique, du département Postes et plus précisément, du service APS (Appareillages de postes et PSEM), composé de 15 personnes. Au Département Poste de la Direction Technique, le Pôle Appareillages de Poste et PSEM (poste sous enveloppe métallique) couvre tout le cycle de vie des disjoncteurs, sectionneurs, parafoudres et postes sous enveloppes métalliques. Il assure la veille technologique, la spécification, la qualification ainsi que la gestion des actifs de ces matériels. Le contexte du stage : Pour faciliter des travaux sous tension, RTE souhaite développer un outil capable de fermer et d’ouvrir des lignes sous tension à vide jusqu’à 420 kV. Lors des manœuvres d’ouverture de ces lignes, l’outil devra être capable de couper un courant de quelques dizaines d’Ampères, généré principalement par les couplages capacitifs phase/phase ou phase/terre. Par ailleurs, après chaque coupure, l’appareil doit être capable de tenir la différence de potentiel entre le réseau et la ligne sous tension à vide, appelée tension de rétablissement. Cette tension, qui apparaitra après chaque coupure, dépend de plusieurs paramètres tels que la configuration de la ligne (simple terne ou double ternes), la tension du réseau, la position où l’appareil de coupure est installé etc. L’objectif principal de ce stage est de caractériser les contraintes de courant et de tension lors des manœuvres de l’appareil de coupure. Les principales missions qui vous seront confiées sont : Recenser les lignes 245 kV et 420 kV « à 3 extrémités ». Le besoin de manœuvrer à vide concerne cette configuration de ligne. Sur les lignes identifiées, rechercher les paramètres des lignes aériennes (par exemple : distance entre phases, distance à la terre, présence de câble de garde …), et définir des configurations types si possible. Pour chaque configuration type identifiée, calculer par simulation le courant à vide et la tension de rétablissement. Le logiciel utilisé par RTE pour le faire est EMTP. Etudier la sensibilité des résultats : avec chaque configuration, la sensibilité des résultats peut être étudiée en variant la tension du réseau, la proximité avec des autres ouvrages du réseau, la longueur de la ligne sous tension à vide etc. Proposer un guide d’utilisation de l’outil en fonction de ses limites et contraintes courant/tension identifiées.

Vous êtes actuellement étudiant en BAC+4 (Master 1) ou BAC+ 5 (Master 2, école d'ingénieur), spécialité Electrotechnique. Vos qualités : Esprit analytique, Bonne communication orale et écrite, Bonne capacité de synthèse, Vous faites preuve d'autonomie et vous êtes capable de travailler en transversalité.

Dans le cadre des activités relatives à l’emploi proposé, vous pouvez être amené(e) à accéder à un (ou des) site(s) relevant de la responsabilité de RTE. A cette fin et dans le respect des articles R1332-22-1 et suivants du Code de la Défense, nous vous informons qu’une enquête administrative est susceptible d’être réalisée à notre demande par l’autorité administrative, afin de vérifier qu’aucun fait vous concernant n’est incompatible avec l’accès envisagé.

Donnez la bonne énergie à votre avenir, formez-vous avec RTE ! RTE est le gestionnaire du réseau français de transport d’électricité. En charge du plus grand réseau haute et très haute tension d’Europe, nous avons la responsabilité de garantir à plus de 67 millions de consommateurs, aux industries et aux distributeurs, une alimentation électrique fiable, 24h/24. En coulisse, plus de 10 000 hommes et femmes orchestrent en temps réel l’équilibre entre production et consommation d’électricité, conduisent les flux, réalisent la maintenance des installations, innovent, mais aussi pilotent les projets qui transforment le réseau, main dans la main avec les territoires. Notre moteur collectif : mettre nos expertises au service de l’intérêt général et d’un futur durable où l’électricité sera la principale énergie. RTE place la santé et la sécurité de ses collaborateurs, prestataires et partenaires au premier plan, en faisant de la prévention des risques un pilier de sa culture d’entreprise. Convaincus que la diversité est une richesse, nous étudions toutes les candidatures avec la même attention, y compris celles de personnes en situation de handicap, pour construire des équipes représentatives d’une société pleinement inclusive. Investi d'une mission de service public, RTE respecte le principe de neutralité religieuse et politique.

description:
During your thesis, you delve into physics-based models of electric drives and our Python component library while simultaneously reviewing current literature on robust system identification and the design of experiments. Furthermore, you develop innovative robustness diagnostics for our existing identification pipeline - considering parameter identifiability, sensitivity, and convergence behavior - and implement as well as quantify appropriate countermeasures. In Addition, you analyze the excitation content of given datasets, evaluate relevant criteria, and link these insights to the achievable identification quality. You comprehensively evaluate the approach you have developed using a practical benchmark use case. Moreover, you document as well as present your research findings clearly and understandably. Lastly, you extend the approach to address partially observable effects resulting from states that cannot be measured directly, such as temperatures.

description:
During contact and relative motion of technical surfaces, energy is dissipated through mechanisms such as plastic deformation, particle generation, surface oxidation, film shearing and heat. From an engineering perspective, it is important to understand whether and under which conditions (materials, surface finish, operating conditions, etc.) the resulting running-in state is stable. The relative contribution of these processes determines the evolving surface topography and health of a tribological contact. You will begin your thesis with a literature review of entropy-based approaches for describing wear and running-in processes. Building on contact mechanics models developed in our department, leading-edge experimental methods and the identified literature, you will then conceptualize and model the surface state after running-in. Finally, you will critically assess the applicability and potential of entropy-based methods for improving the understanding and modelling of running-in in tribological contacts.

description:
Rattaché·e au Département Structure de la Direction Technique, vous contribuez au développement de méthodologies et d'outils pour l'aide au dimensionnement du Containment System (CS) des cuves de stockage cryogénique du gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL). Ces cuves équipent principalement les méthaniers, mais également des navires propulsés au GNL. Dans l'objectif principal d'optimiser et de fiabiliser les études en fatigue des différents systèmes d'isolation GTT, vous déterminerez la contribution des effets thermiques externes ainsi que l'effet de potentiels retraits de soudure sur les déformations de la coque et leur impact sur les systèmes d'isolation. Pour cela, vous aurez à établir un plan de validation comprenant l'étude du navire, la détermination de profils de vie pertinents et l'analyse en fatigue des systèmes d'isolation. Vous serez amené·e à faire des calculs FEM (solveur Abaqus) sur des modèles de navires complets que vous adapterez à vos besoins. Pour les effets thermiques, vous devrez définir des cas de charge réalistes en vous basant sur des données météo. Pour les soudures, vous devrez étudier les différents types de soudures utilisées pour la construction du navire et les modéliser en prenant en compte les énergies de soudage et les températures. Ces calculs vous permettront de définir les déplacements imposés aux systèmes d'isolation. Puis vous déterminerez les zones critiques des systèmes et l'impact de ces déplacements sur ces zones. Enfin, vous déterminerez l'endommagement sur la durée de vie du navire en prenant en compte tous les éléments y contribuant.

description_excerpt: C -TEC INTERNSHIP OFFER Microstructure Engineering and Mechanical Performance of Aluminium Alloys Constellium is a world leader in the development and manufacture of high value-added aluminum products and solutions for a wide range of markets and applications, focusing in particular on aerospace, au
description: C -TEC INTERNSHIP OFFER Microstructure Engineering and Mechanical Performance of Aluminium Alloys Constellium is a world leader in the development and manufacture of high value-added aluminum products and solutions for a wide range of markets and applications, focusing in particular on aerospace, automotive and packaging. Constellium also has nearly 12,000 employees worldwide.We are committed to minimizing the environmental impact of our operations and improving the life cycle footprint of aluminum throughout the value chain. In our company, safety is essential, it is one of our core values without compromise. Our Research and Technology Center, C-TEC Constellium Technology Center, based in Grenoble (Voreppe – 38) employs about 240 people. By joining our company, you will discover a multicultural company (over 20 nationalities) which is committed to diversity and the well-being of its employees. Your mission : Impact of crystallographic texture orientation and its spatial distribution on mechanical performance of Al alloys for automotive – modeling approach Context Due to its low density, aluminium (Al) is a key material for sustainability as it allows lightweighting. To decrease the CO2 emissions associated with its production, it is required to massively use recycled aluminium, meaning remelting Al scrap to make new ingots. However, switching from primary synthesis (bauxite reduction) to secondary synthesis (scrap melting) often leads to increasing impurities, the main one being iron in aluminium. Such contaminants may impact the performance of the current alloys in terms of ductility/formability,. It is the case for the hemming of automotive outer panels. The latter are bent around the inner part after stamping to ensure mechanical assembly. The project of the internship is linked to microstructure optimization, and especially crystallographic texture (meaning grain orientations and their spatial arrangement) to mitigate the detrimental effects of impurities. Thus, it is key to identify how grain microstructure could be tuned to maintain current product performance, while increasing recycled content. For that, Constellium C-TEC has integrated within its modeling tools an open-source software, Damask, allowing to model the mechanical behavior of grains aggregates under different loading types, including tension and bending. A model combining Finite Element Modeling (FEM) and Crystal Plasticity (Damask) has been developed. Up to now, the simulations are performed on a Representative Volume Element (RVE) of the material (hundreds of microns size) which is built with two constraints: mean grain size and grain orientations. No spatial position and size is imposed for each texture component. Objective The main topic of this internship is to model explicitly a spatial distribution of orientations, using experimental data coming from EBSD (Electron BackScatter Diffraction), DCT (Diffraction Contrast Tomography) and XRD (X-ray diffraction) measurements to understand how this spatial distribution can impact the mechanical response of the material, both the plastic anisotropy (yield surface) and the strain localization during loading. . Tensile loading will be a first case of application, particularly relevant for surface defects appearing during stamping (roping). And the model will then be extended to the more complex case of bending. The project has several components The role of the intern will consist, after a first phase of training in our trades and tools, to do : Literature review on methods to transpose microstructure measurements to numerical spatially arranged RVE. X-Ray diffraction (XRD) measurements to measure global crystallographic texture, together with Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) to assess spatial arrangement of grain orientations. Building of a numerical twin of the microstructure to be loaded within Damask software and FEM software (Marc). Handling of the existing numerical models: mainly tensile and bending ones. Some minor changes may be brought by the intern. Study of the impact of spatial arrangement on surface plasticity prediction, strain localization in tension (roping defect) and bending. Comparison between simulations and experiments for identifying which type of texture should be promoted to enhance performance. Analysis and synthesis of the results, report writing and presentation to the team. At C-TEC, the intern will be part of an R&D team of engineers with expertise in metallurgy and mechanics and will be in relation with partners handling the experimental aspects of the investigations. Interaction with an academic expert of crystal plasticity (SIMaP laboratory) is part of the project. Profile Education level: Bac+5 / . ### **Job Title**

**Duration:** minimum 6 months

**Weekly Presence:** 40h (minimum 32h)

**Location:** Eindhoven

**Internship: Robot-Assisted Toothbrush IMU Validation**

Different toothbrushes use inertial measurement units (IMUs) to characterise brushing motion. To compare their measurements fairly, each brush should undergo the same physical motion. In this assignment, you will develop a repeatable test bench combining a 6-DOF robot arm (SeeedStudio reBot Arm B601-RS), OptiTrack motion capture system and toothbrush IMU sensors. Human brushing trajectories, recorded at 120 Hz as position and orientation data, will be transformed into safe robot trajectories and replayed. OptiTrack will independently measure the reproduced motion, enabling quantitative comparison of robot accuracy, repeatability and IMU responses across toothbrushes.

Your challenge: Build and validate a measurement protocol that separates true motion differences from sensor effects such as axis conventions, offset, scale, noise, filtering and timing.

Your team: You will work in the R&D department of Philips Oral Healthcare in Eindhoven, alongside experts in sensors, data science, robotics and oral healthcare. The project combines hands-on experimentation, software development and quantitative signal analysis.

**Your role:**

* Commission the Jetson/ROS 2 robot and OptiTrack workflow and implement safe trajectory replay.
* Define the brush-head TCP and calibrate robot, OptiTrack, marker and IMU coordinate frames.
* Design static and dynamic tests: ±X/±Y/±Z orientations and motions, plus roll/pitch/yaw at several speeds.
* Convert recorded poses and quaternions into continuous, limit-checked robot trajectories.
* Synchronise OptiTrack and IMU data; quantify replay accuracy, repeatability and cross-brush similarity.
Deliver reusable software, a validated protocol and a technical report.

**You're the right fit if:**

* MSc student or last year BSc in Robotics, Mechatronics, Mechanical/Electrical/Biomedical Engineering, Applied Physics, Computer Science or Data Science.
* Python programming and confidence working in Linux.
* Basic linear algebra, 3D rotations and signal-processing skills.
* Affinity with hands-on experiments and systematic validation.
* ROS 2, robot arms, OptiTrack or IMU experience is a plus.
* Good written and spoken English.
Independent, safety-conscious and collaborative.

description: Bull c’est une histoire. Un siècle d’innovation Européenne et un environnement de travail où des experts conçoivent des solutions numériques puissantes, durables et souveraines, permettant aux États et aux industries de garder la pleine maîtrise de leurs données et de leur IA. Chaque jour, nos équipes repoussent les limites du possible - des architectures HPC de nouvelle génération aux supercalculateurs exascale - soutenues par une R&D de rang mondial, plus de 1 600 brevets et des capacités de bout en bout uniques, couvrant la conception matérielle, l’ingénierie logicielle, la data science et la recherche quantique. Contexte du stage : Le poste se situe dans le département R&D logiciel de Bull localisé à Echirolles, au sein du domaine SMC xScale & Inventory. La mission du domaine est de développer des produits logiciels pour le déploiement et le maintien en conditions opérationnelles des supercalculateurs pour l’IA et la simulation numérique. Les équipes R&D utilisent la méthodologie Agile/Scrum. L’accent sera mis sur la modélisation et la simulation des différentes BMC, porte d’entrée pour l’administration d’un tel environnement. Le stagiaire sera en charge de la conception et du développement de la solution logicielle qui devra répondre à des besoins fonctionnels établis. Les perspectives d’évolution de la solution au-delà du cadre initialement défini devront être au cœur des raisonnements et choix d’architecture. Les capacités de mise à l’échelle et la rationalisation des connaissances étant essentielles, Kubernetes et les déploiements de conteneurs sont privilégiés comme cible d’exécution. Les approches de développement micro-service et Cloud Native sont attendues en accord avec l’état de l’art. Les travaux réalisés contribueront de manière structurante aux futurs choix d’évolutions de la plateforme SMC xScale dont le rôle primaire est l’administration et l’exploitation de cluster. La liste de tâches suivantes est un exemple (non exhaustif) des missions qui pourront être réalisées durant la période de stage : · Étude de solution existante et mise en perspective face au besoin fonctionnel · Analyse de leurs limites dans le cadre d’une simulation à grande échelle · Conception et développement logiciel · Réalisation de Proof of Concept · Propositions d’évolutions et de perspectives · Participation à l’intégration et au déploiement de la solution. Compétences appréciées · Kubernetes · Framework Java de développement micro-service (Springboot, Quarkus, ...) · Connaissances de l’écosystème des BMC et en particulier Redfish · Vous faites preuve de curiosité, d'autonomie et de capacités à travailler en équipe.

description:
GTT développe des systèmes d’isolation à destination des bacs de stockage terrestre de liquide cryogénique. Ces bacs sont équipés d’un dôme hémisphérique en partie haute à travers lequel des échanges thermiques radiatifs et convectifs couplés ont lieu. La modélisation précise de ces phénomènes thermiques dépendant du flux thermique, du gradient de température, de la géométrie du bac et de la hauteur de la couche de gaz nécessite des simulations CFD coûteuses en temps et peu adaptées à des calculs itératifs. GTT souhaite mettre en place des outils de calcul précis et rapides de ces échanges thermiques afin d’optimiser le temps d’ingénierie et adresser la performance globale au plus juste. L’objectif est de créer des modèles de corrélations internes (abaques) d’après les conditions thermiques soumises au bac ainsi que ses configurations géométriques.

Compétences techniques : Compétence en simulation CFD 3D, idéalement ANSYS Fluent. Niveau d'études et d'expérience : Élève ingénieur en mécanique des fluides. description:
Contexte Les modèles numériques hydrodynamiques permettent de représenter avec précision les écoulements en rivière et en estuaire. Ils peuvent toutefois nécessiter des temps de calcul importants lorsqu’il s’agit d’explorer un grand nombre de configurations, de produire rapidement des prévisions ou de tester différents scénarios d’aménagement et de fonctionnement. Les méthodes d’intelligence artificielle offrent la possibilité de construire des modèles de substitution , ou surrogate models , capables de reproduire certaines sorties d’un modèle hydrodynamique avec un temps de calcul très réduit. Ces approches peuvent être uniquement fondées sur les données ou intégrer, à différents niveaux, les lois physiques régissant les écoulements. Objectif du stage L’objectif du stage est de développer et d’évaluer une approche d’intelligence artificielle capable de prédire rapidement certaines grandeurs hydrodynamiques caractéristiques d’une rivière ou d’un estuaire, à partir d’une base de simulations numériques ou de données existantes. Approches étudiées Plusieurs familles de modèles pourront être comparées : Un réseau de neurones fondé sur les données , utilisé comme approche de référence ; Une approche de type Physics-Informed Neural Network, ou PINN , intégrant explicitement certaines équations physiques ainsi que des conditions initiales ou aux limites, sous réserve de sa faisabilité dans le cadre du stage ; Une approche hybride ou un modèle de substitution physiquement contraint , constituant une solution intermédiaire si la mise en œuvre d’un PINN complet s’avère trop coûteuse, trop complexe ou difficile à entraîner. Vos missions Votre tuteur accompagnera votre progression sur les missions suivantes : réaliser une revue bibliographique ; identifier et préparer un cas d’application en rivière ou en estuaire , pouvant notamment s’appuyer sur un modèle TELEMAC existant ; constituer et structurer une base de données d’apprentissage et de validation ; développer une première approche fondée uniquement sur les données , utilisée comme modèle de référence ; explorer, selon l’avancement du stage, une approche PINN ou hybride physiquement contrainte , permettant d’introduire certaines connaissances physiques dans l’apprentissage ; quantifier les performances en termes de précision, robustesse et temps de calcul ; identifier les domaines d’application et les limites ; synthétiser la démarche, les résultats et les recommandations. Votre équipe Le stage sera réalisé au sein d’ ArteLab Numérique , l’équipe d’Hydraulique Numérique d’ARTELIA. Cette équipe de 15 personnes réunit des ingénieurs et spécialistes de la modélisation numérique , travaillant sur le développement et l’utilisation de codes de calcul pour la simulation d’écoulements environnementaux et industriels, avec une forte composante hydraulique. Les activités de l’équipe couvrent différentes étapes de la modélisation numérique, depuis le développement, la construction des modèles et leur paramétrage jusqu’à l’exploitation et à l’analyse physique des résultats.

Vos atouts Étudiant en dernière année d’ école d’ingénieur ou Master 2 , avec une spécialisation en hydraulique, mécanique des fluides, modélisation numérique, mathématiques appliquées ou sciences des données . Bonnes bases en hydraulique et mécanique des fluides , permettant de comprendre et d’analyser physiquement les résultats des modèles. Goût pour la modélisation numérique , l’analyse de données et la programmation scientifique. Connaissance de Python et de bibliothèques scientifiques associées. Intérêt marqué pour les méthodes d’ intelligence artificielle et d’apprentissage automatique , notamment les réseaux de neurones. Vous ne travaillez jamais seul, un bon esprit d’équipe, une grande curiosité et l’envie d’apprendre seront vos atouts pour réussir. Qualités personnelles Curiosité scientifique et intérêt pour un sujet à l'interface entre physique, numérique et IA ; esprit critique vis-à-vis des résultats produits par les modèles ; capacité à travailler de manière autonome tout en échangeant avec des spécialistes métier ; rigueur dans l'analyse et la validation des résultats ; capacité à restituer clairement une démarche scientifique et ses limites.

description:
Sous la responsabilité d'Andressa, Directrice technique Génie Civil Nucléaire, vous rejoindrez une équipe dynamique et engagée au service de la transition énergétique. L'objectif de ce stage est de modéliser l’impact d’un avion sur une structure en béton armé (BA), en comparant ses résultats à des données expérimentales disponibles dans la littérature et potentiellement à ceux d’autres logiciels de référence. De plus, l’objectif est aussi de développé un outil de calcul de la loi moment courbure pour une section rectangulaire en BA. Vos missions : Réaliser une étude bibliographique sur la dynamique rapide, les phénomènes d’impact, les essais expérimentaux d’impact avion sur structures en béton armé et les lois nécessaires à l’élaboration de la loi moment-courbure. Analyser les écarts entre les simulations et les résultats expérimentaux ainsi que la sensibilité des paramètres des lois de comportement. Constituer un dossier de validation et de qualification de la loi moment-courbure et des modélisations d’impact avion. description:
Au sein du service Recherche et Développement, vous participerez au développement de joysticks électroniques, à destination du marché du BTP (tractopelles, chargeuses, etc.). Un joystick permet à un utilisateur de piloter les actionneurs de la machine (bras télescopique, godet, etc.) via une commande hydraulique. Un joystick communique avec le calculateur de la machine qu’il pilote via le bus CAN. Toutes les actions du joystick sont pilotées ou supervisées par son logiciel embarqué. Ce logiciel embarqué doit donc être adaptable aux demandes des clients et surtout fiable et sécurisé. Dans cette optique, Bosch Rexroth souhaite améliorer le processus de test de son logiciel embarqué en automatisant un certain nombre de tests. Votre aurez pour mission de : - Développement software : o Automatiser l’analyse des résultats des tests du logiciel embarqué. o Augmenter la couverture de test du logiciel embarqué en codant des tests supplémentaires. o Implémenter le travail réalisé dans une application Orientée Objet codée en C#. Vous devrez vous familiariser avec l’architecture logiciel de notre application de test pour y ajouter de nouvelles fonctionnalités. - Réseaux embarqués o Prendre en main les fonctionnalités de debug et d’espionnage du bus CAN. Vous serez intégré-e dans l’équipe R&D avec une vision globale des différents aspects du développement d’un produit (techniques, financiers, commerciaux, etc.).

Etudiant-e ingénieur en fin de cycle, issu-e d’une formation informatique ou électronique embarqué, vous cherchez un stage de fin d’étude pour une durée de 6 mois. Vous souhaitez acquérir une expérience dans un milieu industriel exigeant. Organisé-e et rigoureux-se, vous faites preuve d'initiative et appréciez le travail en équipe. Vous êtes proactif-ve dans votre travail et êtes en mesure de gérer le bon déroulement d’un projet avec le support de votre tuteur. Vous avez un profil qui apprécie travailler sur le code d’applications haut niveau mais également sur du code plus bas niveau et proche du logiciel embarqué d’un produit. - Vous avez une bonne expérience de la Programmation Orientée Objet. A ce titre la maitrise du C# et/ou de l’IDE Visual studio est un plus. - Vous êtes familier avec la programmation temps réel. - Vous avez une maitrise du développement logiciel qui vous permet de proposer des solutions innovantes à un problème donné. - Avoir travaillé sur des problématiques de tests et validation de logiciel est un atout. - La connaissance des bus embarqué et notamment du bus Can est fortement valorisée.

description: 30 credits Master Thesis – Smart Factory Lab Imitation Learning for Industrial Robots - Development and Evaluation of a Robotic Test Setup Background Applying the latest AI methods to robotics enables the automation of tasks that are currently difficult or impossible to automate. One promising approach is imitation learning, where robots learn complex tasks from human demonstrations instead of being programmed entirely by hand. Scania has already developed an initial proof-of-concept setup together with an external partner. The infrastructure, including an industrial robot, gripper, cameras, computers, and motion-tracking systems, will be provided. The focus of this thesis is on understanding how to effectively train and evaluate robots using imitation learning to support further automation in Scania’s production. The Smart Factory Lab at Scania is an experimental test environment that explores, assesses, and pilots new technologies before they are adopted in Scania’s production processes. We are looking for motivated and creative students to join our Smart Factory Lab for their Master thesis. You will have the opportunity to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, where you can test and validate new technologies, methods, and solutions in close collaboration with our internal and external stakeholders. To learn more about the Smart Factory, visit Link . Assignment The objective is to investigate how different training and data-collection factors influence the performance, robustness, and generalisation of imitation-learned robot policies across relevant industrial use cases. Using the existing robotic test setup, the students will select one or more relevant robot tasks and conduct structured experiments. The work may include: Collecting and preparing demonstration data. Investigating the required amount and variation of demonstrations. Evaluating policy performance on different physical setups and environmental conditions. Documenting the results and developing recommendations for future applications. description:
We are currently seeking a passionate student in their final year of a Master's degree program to join our team for a paid curricular internship opportunity for thesis. As an intern, you will investigate how modern AUTOSAR code generation technologies can be optimized to efficiently operate on resource-constrained embedded platforms. The project will explore the challenges and opportunities of deploying AUTOSAR-based software across a broad range of microcontroller architectures, from low-end devices with tight memory and performance constraints to more capable automotive-grade platforms. The goal of this theis internship is to analyse the assumptions and dependencies embedded in AUTOSAR code generators, identify optimization opportunities, and develop methodologies to improve portability, scalability, and runtime efficiency across different hardware architectures. The project combines software architecture analysis, embedded systems engineering, performance optimization, and practical experimentation. If you are interested in embedded systems, automotive software, code generation technologies, software optimization, and software architecture portability, we encourage you to apply and become part of our dynamic team! You will… Learn about the architecture of modern AUTOSAR Classic code generation toolchains Analyse generated AUTOSAR software and identify optimization opportunities related to memory footprint, CPU utilization, and code size Develop proof-of-concept solutions demonstrating how AUTOSAR components can be optimized for resource-constrained embedded platforms Define a methodology for evaluating software portability and efficiency across different microcontroller architectures Investigate platform-specific assumptions in generated source code and propose architectural improvements Perform measurements and benchmarking activities to assess the impact of different optimization strategies Work together with experienced software developers who will mentor and guide you throughout your journey Have the opportunity for potential full-time employment upon successful completion of the internship

Key qualifications Enrolled in the final year of a university master’s degree program , preferably in Embedded Systems, Software Engineering, Electronic Engineering, or a related field. description: The DLR Institute of Software Technology sees software as a catalyst for research and innovation. The institute's staff, currently numbering around 200, make a significant contribution to advancements in the fields of aviation, space, energy, transportation, and security through the development of state-of-the-art software solutions and innovative research. Our areas of competence include reliable and safety-critical software systems, artificial intelligence, high-performance computing and quantum computing, human-system interaction and visualisation, software and systems engineering as well as digital platforms and digital twins. What to expect In the Flight Software Department, we conduct research and develop reliable and resilient (real-time) software for aircraft and spacecraft. With our expertise in this field, we currently support approximately 20 space missions with software engineering and software quality assurance. This thesis aims to explore the state of the art technologies in Large Language Models, with a focus on investigating the way alternative knowledge representations can improve the capabilities of retrieval-augmented generation algorithms. In current chatbot implementations, capturing the deep semantic structures of extensive technical documentation is a challenge. The project aims to investigate the potential of the newly proposed Open Knowledge Format (OKF) as a framework which preserves the hierarchical structure of domain-specific information. The research investigates opportunities where an AI-aided approach to knowledge management may improve upon classical methods. Dans le cadre du renouvellement de notre gamme de tombereaux miniers, un projet d’envergure a débuté dans le but de définir une nouvelle génération de camions miniers. Nous recherchons un(e) stagiaire pour rejoindre notre équipe d'ingénieurs en mécanique et participer à l’étude et à la définition de l’articulation du train arrière de tombereaux de la gamme Ultra Class. Tâches confiées au stagiaire : Le/la stagiaire intégrera l’équipe OHT LEC, basée à Colmar, et aura en charge la définition, la conception et la standardisation de l’articulation du train arrière de la gamme des camions minier.
